prompt: On GKE, what does a Service of type LoadBalancer produce?

choices.text: An external Application Load Balancer with one global address
choices.why: That is what an Ingress or a Gateway builds.

choices.text: A passthrough Network Load Balancer
choices.why: Right: layer 4, regional, one per Service.

choices.text: Nothing until a Gateway is attached to it
choices.why: The Service alone is enough on GKE.

choices.text: A NodePort reachable only from inside the VPC
choices.why: A NodePort is a different type; LoadBalancer gets an external address.

prompt: The same LoadBalancer manifest leaves EXTERNAL-IP at <pending> on a kind cluster and gets an address on GKE. Why?

choices.text: kind refuses Services of type LoadBalancer
choices.why: The Service is accepted; it just waits.

choices.text: GKE assigns a node's own address to the Service
choices.why: The address belongs to a load balancer outside the cluster.

choices.text: Google builds one on GKE; on kind nobody does
choices.why: Right; the cluster only asks.

choices.text: The manifest needs a cloud annotation that kind ignores
choices.why: No annotation is needed on GKE for an external one.

prompt: Which of these can a passthrough load balancer not do?

choices.text: Carry MQTT traffic to a broker
choices.why: Non-HTTP traffic is exactly what it suits.

choices.text: Offer a service on an address inside the VPC
choices.why: One annotation makes it internal.

choices.text: Forward TCP connections to pods
choices.why: That is its whole job.

choices.text: Send /api/orders and / to different Services
choices.why: Right; routing by path needs layer 7.

prompt: The annotation networking.gke.io/load-balancer-type with the value ___ gives a Service an address inside the VPC.
A team deletes and recreates its LoadBalancer Service during a migration, and the site disappears for everyone although the pods are fine. What happened?

choices.text: The pods lost their readiness gate
choices.why: The pods are fine; the front door moved.

choices.text: The address changed, and DNS still has the old one
choices.why: Right; reserve a static address, or use a Gateway on a reserved one.

choices.text: GKE needs a second Service to rebuild the forwarding rule
choices.why: One Service is enough; the address is what changed.

choices.text: The load balancer kept routing to deleted nodes for ever
choices.why: Nodes were not deleted.

prompt: What does the GKE Ingress controller build from an Ingress?

choices.text: An external Application Load Balancer
choices.why: Right: one address, many paths, TLS at Google.

choices.text: One passthrough load balancer per path
choices.why: Paths share one layer-7 load balancer.

choices.text: An nginx Deployment inside the cluster
choices.why: That is another controller; GKE's builds Google's load balancer.

choices.text: A Cloud Run service in front of the pods
choices.why: Cloud Run has no part in it.

prompt: Why is shop-web reserved with Terraform instead of letting the Ingress get an address?

choices.text: An Ingress cannot have an address of its own
choices.why: It can, an ephemeral one.

choices.text: A reserved address is cheaper than an ephemeral one
choices.why: Price is not the argument made.

choices.text: It outlives the Ingress and the cluster
choices.why: Right; DNS points at it once.

choices.text: Terraform validates that the address is free
choices.why: The plan cannot know; the address is assigned on apply.

prompt: A ManagedCertificate stays in Provisioning for hours. What is the usual cause?
hint: How does the authority check the domain?

choices.text: The Ingress has too many paths
choices.why: Paths do not affect the certificate.

choices.text: Google issues certificates only on weekdays
choices.why: Issuance does not depend on the day.

choices.text: The cluster is regional and the certificate global
choices.why: That is the normal arrangement.

choices.text: DNS does not point at the load balancer yet
choices.why: Right; that is how the domain is proved yours.

prompt: How many resources did the plan for lb/address.tf add on its own?
The external Application Load Balancer needs a ___ address, not a regional one.
What does a network endpoint group list, for a load balancer on GKE?

choices.text: The nodes of the cluster and their node ports
choices.why: That is the old path, through instance groups.

choices.text: Pod addresses and ports
choices.why: Right; requests go straight to pods.

choices.text: The Services in a namespace
choices.why: A Service is a backend; its pods are the endpoints.

choices.text: The certificates of the Ingress
choices.why: Certificates live on the target proxy.

prompt: With node backends, a node runs one broken pod among healthy ones. What does the load balancer see?
hint: What does the health check test there?

choices.text: The broken pod, which it removes at once
choices.why: With node backends it does not see pods.

choices.text: An unhealthy node, which it removes
choices.why: The node passes, because most of it is fine.

choices.text: A node that passes, so traffic keeps arriving
choices.why: Right; NEGs move the health check to the pod.

choices.text: Nothing, until kube-proxy reports the pod
choices.why: kube-proxy reports nothing to the load balancer.

prompt: During a rollout, why does the readiness gate GKE adds keep customers from seeing errors?
hint: When does a new pod count as ready?

choices.text: Old pods go only once new ones are healthy in the load balancer
choices.why: Right; Kubernetes waits for the load balancer.

choices.text: It slows every rollout to one pod per minute
choices.why: No fixed pace is imposed.

choices.text: It sends a copy of each request to old and new pods
choices.why: Nothing mirrors requests.

choices.text: It keeps the old ReplicaSet for a soak period
choices.why: That describes blue-green nodes in lesson 13.

prompt: On the old path, the node hands the request to the rules of kube-___, which forward it to a pod.
hint: The component that runs on every node.

prompt: Order the old path of a request through node backends.
items: The load balancer picks a node
The request arrives on the Service's node port
kube-proxy's rules pick a pod, often on another node

prompt: In the Gateway API, which object does each application team write?

choices.text: The GatewayClass
choices.why: Google provides the classes on GKE.

choices.text: The Gateway
choices.why: The platform owns the Gateway.

choices.text: An HTTPRoute, in its namespace
choices.why: Right; it attaches to the platform's Gateway.

choices.text: A ManagedCertificate
choices.why: Certificates sit on the Gateway's listeners.

prompt: What can an HTTPRoute do that an Ingress on GKE never could?

choices.text: Send different paths to different Services
choices.why: Ingress does that too.

choices.text: Split traffic between Services by weight
choices.why: Right; a canary without touching the Gateway.

choices.text: Terminate TLS with a Google-managed certificate
choices.why: Ingress has ManagedCertificate for that.

choices.text: Use a global address
choices.why: Ingress uses one too.

prompt: The route sends weight 90 to orders and 10 to orders-next. Out of 2,000 requests, about how many reach orders-next?
Which value of gateway_api_config.channel did the provider refuse, and why does it matter?
hint: The accepted names carry a prefix.

choices.text: CHANNEL_EXPERIMENTAL, because Autopilot forbids it
choices.why: It was in the accepted list.

choices.text: CHANNEL_STANDARD, because it is the default already
choices.why: It planned cleanly.

choices.text: STANDARD: the names carry the CHANNEL_ prefix
choices.why: Right; the provider listed the three it knows.

choices.text: REGULAR, which belongs to release channels
choices.why: That was lesson 13's field, not this one.

prompt: The GKE class for the global external Application Load Balancer is gke-l7-global-external-___.
Match each need to what the shop should use.

pairs.left: An MQTT broker on the internet
A service offered to virtual machines in the VPC
Many HTTP paths on one domain, each team its own

prompt: The shop has five public HTTP services, each exposed as a Service of type LoadBalancer. What does moving them behind one Gateway change on the bill and in DNS?
hint: Count the load balancers and the addresses.

choices.text: Nothing: a Gateway creates one load balancer per route
choices.why: One Gateway is one load balancer.

choices.text: Five addresses become ten, one per listener and route
choices.why: Listeners share the Gateway's address.

choices.text: Five load balancers and addresses become one of each
choices.why: Right; routes share the Gateway.

choices.text: The services lose TLS, which only Services provide
choices.why: A passthrough Service provides no managed TLS at all.

prompt: Which of these did the lab check in lesson 16? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: That the global address resource is well formed
choices.why: Right; it planned, with the address known after apply.

choices.text: That CHANNEL_STANDARD is an accepted Gateway API channel
choices.why: Right; STANDARD alone was refused.

choices.text: That the HTTPRoute attaches to the Gateway
choices.why: No manifest was applied anywhere.

choices.text: That the certificate was issued for shop.example.com
choices.why: Nothing reached a certificate authority.

prompt: Container-native load balancing is on without being asked for. On which clusters?

choices.text: Only on Standard clusters with Spot nodes
choices.why: Spot has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Only on clusters in the EXTENDED channel
choices.why: Channels decide versions, not this.

choices.text: Only when a Service sets type LoadBalancer
choices.why: It is about Ingress and Gateway backends.

choices.text: Any whose pods get VPC addresses, Autopilot included
choices.why: Right; Ingress and Gateway use NEGs there.
